title: Round 2: experiments on approximate characters and coordinate-predicate bias
question: Run pre-registered, seeded, reproducible experiments on toy curves testing the listed hypotheses with an explicit multiple-testing protocol; report all results including null results.
claims: E-A (empirical, toy domain only): in 24 random prime-order curves (p 547..4481, two seeds) none of 40 low-degree coordinate functions is near-character (min defect 0.499, random level 0.5); positive controls (exact/noisy characters, mixtures >= ~0.1-0.2) are detected.

E-A Fourier: the pre-registered threshold flagged 4 (seed 1) + 1 (seed 2) odd functions (max F/T 1.08, 1.01) because the pre-registered null ignored the symmetry f(-Q)=-f(Q) (real coefficients); a post-hoc symmetry-aware null (verified against matched simulations) gives 0 rejections in both seeds. This is a deviation, not a clean pass.

E-B (empirical, toy domain only): 0 of 2520 tests per seed (2 seeds, 120 curves each, p 1e3..1e5) reject at the Bonferroni level; chi-square tests of independence from k mod m are consistent with uniform p-values.

E-B anomaly, reproduced in both seeds: p-value distributions of DFT-max and lag-1 tests for the Legendre predicates chi(x), chi(y) are far from uniform (pooled KS p ~1e-12), the sequences have a flatter spectrum than random (periodogram variance ~0.66 vs 1) for chi of linear functions of x and for chi(y), not for parity, hash bits, chi(x^2+x+1), chi(xy); order-shuffled controls are fine. Cause unestablished; possible artifact not excluded. Not a finding until independently confirmed.
No proof or formal result; proof_status not-applicable. No statement about cryptographic sizes.
next_action: PI: decide on E-A post-hoc symmetric null (clean option: third fresh seed with corrected pre-registered null); investigate the E-B Legendre-predicate spectral flatness (exact periodogram variance, independent group-law implementation, full-period sequences with symmetry in the null) before it is reported as a finding.
